harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: WebDAV is operational at http://node1:8080/documents/. The supplied editor account has authenticated CRUD access, exclusive locks reject tokenless overwrites, anonymous access is denied, protected source documents remain unchanged, and all behavior recovered after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL-native Apache HTTP Server 2.4.63 packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created a writable WebDAV workspace at /srv/webdav/documents from the supplied documents.
Configured Basic authentication for editor using the supplied credential, with bcrypt storage and restricted file permissions.
Configured mod_dav_fs locking, SELinux write contexts, firewalld TCP/8080 access, and automatic httpd startup.
Verified authenticated discovery, read, create, replace, delete, exclusive lock enforcement, token-authorized replacement, and anonymous denial.
Removed all temporary test documents and credential files.
Safely restarted node1, proved its boot ID changed, and repeated service, data, authentication, CRUD, and locking checks after recovery.

evidence.requirement: WebDAV workspace available at /documents/ on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Configuration validates; httpd is enabled and active; TCP/8080 is listening and permitted through firewalld.

evidence.requirement: Editor can create, read, replace, and delete documents
evidence.summary: Observed PROPFIND 207, GET 200, create 201, replace 204, delete 204, and matching content before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Exclusive locks prevent overwrite without the lock token
evidence.summary: Exclusive LOCK succeeded; tokenless PUT returned 423 and content remained unchanged; token-authorized PUT returned 204.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous clients cannot access the workspace
evidence.summary: Anonymous access returned HTTP 401 before and after restart; an incorrect password also returned 401.
brief.txt and budget.csv retained identical SHA-256 checksums; access.txt remains root-owned and mode 0600.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel preserved

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 7217fc31-8b1e-4097-936b-13f98cd8a5df was captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 100ae3f5-e958-4dd4-bbb9-672014a395d8; service, listener, firewall, SELinux, source data, authentication, CRUD, and locking all recovered with no failed units.
